## Office of the State Fire Marshal’s Proposed Changes to the Permanently Moored Craft Fire Prevention and Safety Rules (Part 149)

These proposed amendments would clarify and update the regulatory requirements for Permanently Moored Crafts (PMCs) in the State. Specifically, the proposed amendments would modify and clarify the inspection requirements for PMCs. Currently required to be conducted annually, the proposed amendments would instead create a staggered inspection cycle in which the various inspections would be completed across a five-year period, depending on the type of PMC. This addresses concerns raised by the regulated public about the difficulty of meeting current requirements while maintaining a safe and stable structure. The proposed amendments would also update requirements for those who provide these inspections, update referenced standards, and revise and clarify terminology. Overall, the proposed amendments provide additional clarity and direction for the regulated public.

OSFM will be accepting comments during the 45-day public comment period from September 4, 2026 through October 19, 2026. Comments may be e-mailed to SFM.Rules@illinois.gov or sent in writing to:

  *   * # First Notice Period on Proposed Rule Changes to Annual Child Care Eligibility, Maximum Monthly Income and Parent Fee

announcement: – Wednesday, August 5, 2026

Each year, the lead agency for the Illinois Child Care Assistance Program (CCAP) is required to amend the Illinois administrative code to reflect changes implemented as a result of adjusting Illinois’ child care eligibility guidelines and co-payment fees based on the Federal Poverty Level.  

These rates were revised on July 1, 2026 as required by law. 

The revised rates have now been posted as proposed changes within Volume 50, Issue 28 of the Illinois Register. Current rules may be viewed here in 23 Ill. Adm. Code, Sections 2060.230 and 2060.320 (formerly 89 Ill. Adm. Code, Sections 50.230 and 50.320) - Child Care Eligibility and Maximum Monthly Income and Parent Fee. 

As required by the rulemaking process during the State’s First Notice period, IDEC is we are now accepting public comments on this action through August 23, 2026.  

Information on submitting public comment is available in the public register link above. Public comments may also be submitted to DEC.Rules@Illinois.Gov.  All comments, including those submitted to IDHS, will be routed to IDEC to facilitation through the rulemaking process.
